### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, every case ran exactly one of the four alternative activities A14, A15, A20 and A21 (each in about 20–28 of 100 traces) between A41 and A22: all of A41's outgoing transitions went to these four (about 20–28% each), each alternative always led on to A22, and A41 reached A22 in two steps. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR008, LAG004, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004]
- In the later window, A41 leads directly to A22 in one step in all cases, and its transitions to the four alternatives are no longer observed. [DIR008, LAG004]
- The four alternatives now run much later: their mean position moved from about 0.32–0.33 to about 0.59–0.61 of the trace, and their order relative to A22 and A23 reversed — earlier, each preceded A22 and A23 in every case where they co-occurred (about 20–28 of 100 traces, never the reverse); later, each follows them (about 22–27 of 100, never the reverse), while co-occurrence stays at about 20–28 of 100 traces. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008]
- The alternatives are now inserted into the late A23–A24–A28 chain. Earlier, A23 always led to A24 and A24 always to A28, so A23 reached A28 in two steps in every case. Later, A23 goes to A24 in about 52 of 100 of its transitions and to one of the alternatives in about 48 (10–14% each); A24 goes to A28 in about 49 and to an alternative in about 51; each alternative leads to A24 or A28 in roughly equal shares (about 42–58%); A23 reaches A24 in one step in about 52 of 100 cases and in two in about 48, A24 reaches A28 in one step in about 49 and in two in about 51, and A23 reaches A28 in three steps in every case — consistent with exactly one alternative being inserted per case, either before A24 or between A24 and A28. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]
- Minor shifts: A22 and A23 now sit slightly earlier (mean position about 0.35 to 0.32 and 0.59 to 0.56), and the mix among the four alternatives changed a little (A21 from about 20 to 27 of 100 traces, A20 from about 26 to 22). [POS005, POS006, POS003, POS004]
- Separately, at A03 (present in about half of the traces in both windows) the outgoing shares moved from A04 (about 40% to 22%) toward A09 (about 21% to 35%), with A05 roughly stable (about 39% to 43%). [DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the one-per-case alternative block A14/A15/A20/A21 was relocated from the early stage between A41 and A22 to the late stage between A23/A24 and A28: earlier, each case ran A41 → one alternative → A22; later, A41 runs straight to A22 and the chosen alternative is inserted into the A23–A24–A28 sequence, before A24 or between A24 and A28. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008]

The change is shown directly, not inferred from frequency shifts alone: the order between each alternative and A22/A23 flips completely while co-occurrence is unchanged, the successor profiles of A41, A23, A24 and of the four alternatives change accordingly, the alternatives' positions move from about a third to about three fifths of the trace, and the step distances match removal and re-insertion (A41→A22 from two steps to one; A23→A28 from two to three in every case). The 24 items far exceed the roughly 0.4 items expected by chance across the 74 tested units, every item's difference exceeds about 995 of 1000 random re-splits, and the block still runs once per case (its trace shares sum to about 100 of 100 in both windows), which fits a moved block rather than an added, removed or duplicated one. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004]

Limitation: the evidence does not show what A22, A24 or A28 lead to beyond the transitions listed, and it cannot fully rule out that the picture arises from two coordinated but separate routing changes (one at A41, one at A23/A24 together with the four alternatives) rather than a single relocation; the mirrored shares make the relocation reading the more parsimonious one, but a single underlying change is not proven. [DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, LAG002, LAG004]

Other differences: at A03 the choice between existing successors shifted — A04 fell from about 40 to 22 in 100 of A03's outgoing transitions while A09 rose from about 21 to 35 and A05 stayed near four in ten; all involved activities are well observed in both windows, so this looks like existing paths being taken with different frequencies, but it rests on a single indicator and no link to the relocated block is shown. [DIR001]
